Statement: The cinema hall plans to start a separate ticket counter for senior citizens with the aim of making the ticketing process smoother. This indicates an intention to improve convenience or reduce difficulty, not to claim perfection or universal need.

Assumption I: The statement does not assume that all senior citizens need special assistance. Creating a separate counter may be for convenience, prioritization, or comfort, even if only some senior citizens benefit. The word "every" makes the assumption too extreme and therefore not implicit.

Assumption II: The statement only mentions making the process smoother, not eliminating waiting time altogether. There is no claim or hidden belief of complete removal of waiting. Hence, this assumption is not implicit.

So, neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit.

Under the Constitution, legislative powers are divided in the Seventh Schedule into:

Union List

State List

Concurrent List

However, subjects that are not mentioned in any of these three lists fall under Residuary Powers, which belong to Parliament under Article 248 and Entry 97 of the Union List.

Since cyber law and cyberspace issues were not foreseen when the Constitution was drafted, they are not mentioned in the three lists. Therefore, Parliament enacted the Information Technology Act, 2000 using its residuary legislative powers.

Further Insights:

• Article 246 distributes legislative powers between Union and States.

• Article 248 gives Parliament residuary legislative powers.

• Entry 97 of the Union List also covers subjects not listed elsewhere.

• The Information Technology Act, 2000 is India's primary law governing cybercrime, digital signatures, and electronic commerce.

• India later amended the IT Act through the Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008 to address modern cyber threats.

Both statements are historically accurate.

Ajatashatru, the king of Magadha (5th century BCE), fought a prolonged war against the Vrijji (Vajji) confederacy, whose capital was Vaishali. According to Buddhist sources, this conflict lasted around 16 years.

The Vrijjis were a powerful republican confederacy consisting of several clans, including the Licchavis. Because they functioned collectively and had strong internal unity, defeating them militarily was difficult.

Ajatashatru's minister Vassakara used diplomatic and political strategies to weaken the confederacy. He allegedly created divisions among the tribes, weakening their unity. Once their internal cohesion broke down, Magadha was able to defeat them.

Thus, the internal sabotage engineered by Vassakara explains why the war eventually ended in Magadha's victory after a long struggle.

Therefore, both statements are true and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

Further Insights:

• The Vrijji (Vajji) confederacy was one of the Mahajanapadas of ancient India.

• Vaishali, the capital of the Vrijjis, is considered one of the world's earliest republics.

• Ajatashatru is also known for building the fortifications of Rajagriha and strengthening Magadha.

• He reportedly used war machines such as the Mahashilakantaka and Rathamusala during his campaigns.

• The victory over the Vrijjis helped Magadha emerge as the dominant power in northern India, paving the way for later empires like the Nandas and Mauryas.

Nivedita Dubey was appointed as Member (Human Resources) on the Board of the Airports Authority of India (AAI). With this appointment, she became the first woman officer to serve on the AAI Board, marking a historic milestone in the Indian aviation sector.

She took charge on 30 January 2026, after previously serving as Regional Executive Director (Eastern Region) of AAI, where she managed multiple airports and administrative functions.

Further Insights:

• The Airports Authority of India (AAI) functions under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

• AAI manages over 130 airports across India.

• The organization is responsible for airport infrastructure and air navigation services.

• AAI was formed in 1995 through the merger of International Airports Authority of India and National Airports Authority.

The Harmika is a small square railing-like structure placed on top of the hemispherical dome (Anda) of a Buddhist stupa. It symbolizes the abode of the gods (devaloka) and marks the sacred space above the relic mound. From the Harmika rises the central pillar (Yasti) which supports the Chhatra (umbrella discs) representing spiritual hierarchy.

Further Insights:

• The Anda (dome) symbolizes the cosmic egg and the burial mound of Buddha's relics.

• The Yasti (central pillar) rising from the Harmika represents the axis mundi or cosmic axis.

• The Chhatra (umbrella discs) symbolize royalty, protection, and spiritual rank.

• Famous stupas with elaborate Toranas include the Sanchi Stupa in Madhya Pradesh.

• Pradakshina patha around the stupa is used by devotees to circumambulate in a clockwise direction.

Excellent dielectric strength (good electrical insulation)

Low power loss factor

The Teesta River flows through the Siliguri Corridor in northern West Bengal, which is a narrow stretch of land connecting mainland India to the Northeastern states. Because of its location, the river is strategically important for transport, infrastructure, water management, and security logistics in the region.

Further Insights:

• It connects eight northeastern states with mainland India.

• The corridor lies between Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, and China (Tibet).

• The Teesta River originates from the Tso Lhamo Lake in Sikkim.

Matangini Hazra was a freedom fighter from Bengal who actively participated in the Quit India Movement in 1942. She was popularly called "Gandhi Buri" because of her dedication to Mahatma Gandhi's ideals.

In Tamluk (Midnapore district), she led a procession of protesters carrying the Indian national flag. During the protest, British police opened fire, and she was shot. Even after being hit by bullets, she continued chanting "Vande Mataram" until she died.

Aruna Asaf Ali

Aruna Asaf Ali is famous for hoisting the Indian National Flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai during the Quit India Movement

Kalpana Datta

Pritilata Wadedar

Pritilata Wadedar was a revolutionary associated with the Chittagong movement and died after the Pahartali European Club attack in 1932.

Further Insights:

• Matangini Hazra was about 73 years old when she was martyred.

• The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942.

• Tamluk in Bengal later became the center of the Tamralipta National Government, a parallel government formed by freedom fighters.

• Matangini Hazra was an active participant in the Civil Disobedience Movement before 1942.

Aditya Pandya, a 17-year-old space enthusiast, became India's youngest male analog astronaut after completing an eight-day lunar simulation mission in Dholavira, Kutch (Gujarat) from 1 - 8 February 2026. The mission simulated Moon-like isolation and habitat conditions on Earth.

The mission was conducted by AAKA Space Studio, where a small crew lived in a container-based lunar habitat to test human survival, system reliability, and psychological endurance under simulated space conditions.

Further Insights:

• Analog astronaut missions simulate Moon or Mars conditions on Earth for research and training.

• The 2026 mission took place in Dholavira (Rann of Kutch, Gujarat) due to its desert terrain resembling lunar landscapes.

• The mission was conducted by AAKA Space Studio, a registered ISRO Space Tutor organization.

• Analog missions help prepare for future human spaceflight programmes like Gaganyaan.

During Akbar's reign, a special translation bureau called Maktab Khana (House of Translation) was established at Fatehpur Sikri.

The purpose was to translate important Sanskrit and regional texts into Persian, the administrative language of the Mughal Empire.

Abdul Qadir Badauni was commissioned to translate the Ramayana into Persian. Although Badauni personally disagreed with Akbar's religious policies, he still carried out the translation work assigned to him.

Abul Fazl

Abul Fazl was Akbar's chief court historian and wrote Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari, but he was not responsible for translating the Ramayana.

Faizi

Faizi translated several Sanskrit works and was involved in the translation of Lilavati (a mathematical text), but not the Ramayana.

Dara Shikoh

Dara Shikoh lived later during Shah Jahan's reign and translated the Upanishads into Persian (Sirr-i-Akbar).

Further Insights:

• Akbar established the Maktab Khana (translation bureau) at Fatehpur Sikri in 1574.

• The Mahabharata was translated into Persian as "Razmnama."

• Akbar promoted the policy of Sulh-i-Kul (universal peace) to encourage religious tolerance.

• Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari, important sources for Mughal history.

• Dara Shikoh later translated the Upanishads into Persian, reflecting Mughal interest in Indian philosophy.

The Suresh Tendulkar Committee was constituted by the Planning Commission of India in 2005 under the chairmanship of economist Suresh Tendulkar. Its primary objective was to review and suggest improvements in the methodology used to estimate poverty in India.

The committee submitted its report in 2009 and recommended a new method of calculating the poverty line, moving away from the older calorie-based approach. Instead, it incorporated expenditure on health, education, and other essential needs into the poverty estimation framework.

Further Insights:

• The Tendulkar Committee Report was submitted in 2009 to the Planning Commission.

• It replaced the earlier Lakdawala Committee poverty estimation method (1993).

• According to the Tendulkar methodology, 21.9% of India's population was below the poverty line in 2011 - 12.

• Later, the Rangarajan Committee (2014) proposed another method for estimating poverty.

The memoir "Four Stars of Destiny" was written by General Manoj Mukund Naravane, the 28th Chief of the Army Staff of India, who served from December 2019 to April 2022.

The book discusses his four-decade military career, including key events such as the Galwan Valley clash with China, military leadership challenges, and defence policies.

The memoir became controversial because excerpts reportedly circulated before official clearance, and the publisher clarified that the book has not yet been officially published.

Further Insights:

• General M. M. Naravane served as the 28th Chief of the Army Staff (2019 - 2022).

• His tenure included the 2020 Galwan Valley clash between India and China.

• The book reportedly discusses military strategy, leadership, and border conflicts.

• The publisher Penguin Random House India holds the publishing rights to the memoir.

A Production Possibility Curve (PPC) shows the maximum combinations of two goods that an economy can produce using its available resources.

When the PPC is concave (bowed outward), it indicates increasing opportunity cost.

This happens because resources are not perfectly adaptable for producing different goods.

As more units of one good are produced, increasing amounts of the other good must be sacrificed, causing opportunity cost to rise.

Constant Opportunity Cost

Constant opportunity cost produces a straight-line PPC, not a curved one.

Decreasing Opportunity Cost

If opportunity cost decreased, the curve would bend inward, which is not typical in economic theory.

Zero Opportunity Cost

Zero opportunity cost would imply unlimited resources, which contradicts the basic economic problem of scarcity.

Further Insights:

• The Production Possibility Curve (PPC) represents the concept of scarcity and choice in economics.

• A straight-line PPC indicates constant opportunity cost.

• Points inside the PPC represent inefficient use of resources.

• Points on the PPC represent efficient production levels.

• Points outside the PPC are unattainable with current resources and technology.

Indian badminton player Devika Sihag won the women's singles title at the Thailand Masters 2026, which is a BWF World Tour Super 300 event. She secured the title after Malaysia's Goh Jin Wei retired during the final, while Sihag was leading the match.

This victory marked her maiden BWF Super 300 title and made her one of the few Indian women to win a World Tour title at this level.

Further Insights:

• The Thailand Masters is part of the BWF World Tour Super 300 circuit.

• The 2026 edition was held at Nimibutr Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand.

• The tournament had a total prize pool of USD 250,000.

• Devika Sihag became one of the few Indian women to win a Super 300 title, joining players like Saina Nehwal and PV Sindhu.

• The BWF World Tour includes categories such as Super 1000, Super 750, Super 500, and Super 300.

Lai Haraoba is an important religious and cultural festival of the Meitei people of Manipur. The term literally means "Merrymaking of the Gods."

During this festival, rituals, dances, and traditional performances are conducted to honor the Umang Lai (forest deities). The ceremonies symbolically recreate the story of the creation of the universe, including the origin of life, nature, and human society.

The ritual dances performed by Maibis (priestesses) depict different stages of cosmic creation and cultural traditions of the Meitei community.

Sangai Festival

The Sangai Festival is a modern cultural and tourism festival organized by the Government of Manipur to promote tourism, culture, and the state's heritage.

Kang Rath Yatra

Kang Rath Yatra in Manipur is associated with the Jagannath tradition of Hinduism, similar to the Rath Yatra celebrated in Puri. It involves pulling a chariot of Lord Jagannath and is unrelated to Umang Lai worship.

Yaoshang

Yaoshang is the Manipuri version of the Holi festival, celebrated with sports events, dance, and cultural activities.

Further Insights:

• Umang Lai refers to the sacred forest deities worshipped in Manipur.

• The ritual dances of Lai Haraoba are performed mainly by priestesses called Maibis.

• Ras Lila, another famous dance tradition of Manipur, is associated with Vaishnavism.

• The Sangai deer, the state animal of Manipur, is found in KeibulLamjao National Park.

• Yaoshang festival in Manipur lasts five days and coincides with the Hindu festival of Holi.

• The Council of Ministers includes Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.

Newton's Law of Cooling describes the rate of heat loss of a body due to convection.

According to this law, the rate of heat transfer between a surface and the surrounding fluid is proportional to the temperature difference between them.

Where:

Fourier's Law

Wien's Displacement Law

Wien's Law relates to thermal radiation, specifically the relationship between temperature and the wavelength of maximum radiation emitted by a black body.

The Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007 - 2012) adopted the theme "Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth."

The main aim of this plan was to ensure that economic growth benefits all sections of society, particularly the poor, rural population, women, and marginalized communities.

The plan focused on sectors such as:

Education

Health

Agriculture

Infrastructure

Employment generation

Further Insights:

• India's First Five-Year Plan began in 1951 under the Planning Commission.

• The Eleventh Plan targeted an average GDP growth rate of about 9%.

• It emphasized expansion of education through schemes like Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan.

• The Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012 - 2017) was the last Five-Year Plan of India.

The nickname "Payyoli Express" actually belongs to P. T. Usha, the legendary Indian sprinter from Payyoli, Kerala. She earned this nickname due to her exceptional speed in track events, especially in the 1980s Asian competitions and the 1984 Olympics.

K. D. Jadhav was an Indian wrestler who won India's first individual Olympic medal at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics (bronze in wrestling). However, he was not known by the nickname "Payyoli Express."

• Milkha Singh won four gold medals at the 1958 Asian Games and Commonwealth Games.

• Karnam Malleswari won a bronze medal at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, India's first Olympic medal by a woman.

• K. D. Jadhav won India's first individual Olympic medal in 1952.

• Pankaj Advani has won multiple world titles in both billiards and snooker formats.

Under the PM RAHAT Scheme, the Government of India provides cashless medical treatment up to ₹1.5 lakh per road accident victim. The treatment coverage is available for up to seven days from the date of the accident in designated hospitals.

The scheme aims to ensure that no accident victim is denied life-saving treatment due to lack of money, especially during the "Golden Hour", when prompt medical care can save lives.

Further Insights:

• PM RAHAT stands for Road Accident Victim Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment.

• It was launched by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) in 2026.

• The scheme focuses on providing medical care during the "Golden Hour" after accidents.

• It is linked with the 112 Emergency Response Support System (ERSS).

• Claims are processed digitally through the eDAR (Electronic Detailed Accident Report) system and National Health Authority platforms.

The Kamarupa dynasty, located in present-day Assam in Northeast India, was not involved in the Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj. Its political activities were mainly concentrated in the Brahmaputra Valley region, and it did not compete for control of Kannauj.

The Tripartite Struggle (8th - 10th century CE) was a long political conflict among three major powers for dominance over Kannauj, a strategically and economically important city in northern India.

The three main contenders were:

The Palas of Bengal

The Gurjara-Pratiharas of western and northern India

The Rashtrakutas of the Deccan

Further Insights:

• Kannauj became politically important after the decline of Harsha's empire.

• The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala around 750 CE.

• Mihira Bhoja was one of the greatest rulers of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty.

• The Rashtrakutas ruled from Manyakheta in present-day Karnataka.

• The Kamarupa kingdom was one of the earliest historical states of Northeast India, ruling the Brahmaputra Valley.

VeerapandiyaKattabomman was the Polygar (Palayakkarar) chieftain of Panchalankurichi in present-day Tamil Nadu. He strongly opposed the East India Company's demand for tribute (tax).

His resistance led to the First Polygar War (1799) between the British and several Polygar chieftains. After being captured by the British, Kattabomman was executed at Kayathar on 16 October 1799.

Further Insights:

• The Polygar (Palayakkarar) system was a local administrative system in South India during the Nayak period.

• The First Polygar War took place in 1799 between the British and local chieftains of Tamil Nadu.

• The Second Polygar War (1800 - 1801) involved wider resistance led by the Maruthu brothers.

• VeerapandiyaKattabomman became a symbol of early resistance against British colonial rule in South India.

The Sarda Act, also known as the Child Marriage Restraint Act (1929), fixed the minimum marriage age at 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys. It was introduced by Harbilas Sarda.

Further Insights:

• The Sarda Act (1929) is also known as the Child Marriage Restraint Act.

• The Age of Consent Act (1891) was partly triggered by the Phulmoni Dasi case.

• Harbilas Sarda, a judge and legislator, introduced the Sarda Bill in the Central Legislative Assembly.

• The Brahmo Samaj played a major role in promoting social reforms in marriage practices.

• After independence, the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 further strengthened laws against child marriage in India.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech in: "Wonderful timing!" he said, as the printer jammed during the deadline.
questions.questionHtml: Identify the figure of speech in: "Wonderful timing!" he said, as the printer jammed during the deadline.
questions.solution:
Correct option is Irony (Option a) because the words ("wonderful timing") mean the opposite of the real situation (bad timing).

Irony means saying something that clashes with the actual situation for effect.

Example: "Great job!" when someone has clearly made a mistake.

Option b Hyperbole is wrong because the key feature is opposite-meaning, not exaggeration.

Option c Personification is wrong because no non-living thing is given a human action here.

Option d Alliteration is wrong because there is no repeated starting sound pattern.

Final sentence: "Wonderful timing!" he said, as the printer jammed during the deadline.

questions.question: Fill the correct degree of comparison: Among all the applicants interviewed today, Riya gave the ____ response to the case-study question.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill the correct degree of comparison:

Among all the applicants interviewed today, Riya gave the ____ response to the case-study question.
questions.solution:
Option c is correct because "among all" shows comparison with more than two, so we need the superlative "sharpest."

Rule (Degree of Comparison): Use superlative form when comparing three or more items, usually with "the/among/of all."

Example: "Of all the desserts, this is the sweetest."

· Option a is wrong because "sharper" is comparative (used for two).

· Option b is wrong because "sharp" is the base form and does not show "most."

· Option d is wrong because "more sharp" is incorrect; "sharp" takes "sharper/sharpest."

Final correct sentence: Among all the applicants interviewed today, Riya gave the sharpest response to the case-study question.

questions.question: Choose the option that gives the correct passive form of the sentence. The technician has been updating the phone's software for two hours.

Choose the option that gives the correct passive form of the sentence.

The technician has been updating the phone's software for two hours.

options.text: The phone's software has updated by the technician for two hours.

options.html: The phone's software was being updated by the technician for two hours.

questions.solution:
Option (b) is correct because the active sentence is in Present Perfect Continuous ("has been updating"). In passive, Present Perfect Continuous becomes "has/have been being + past participle". So "has been updating" changes to "has been being updated".

Rule of Voice Transformation: Keep the tense same; move the object to subject position; use the correct "be" form + V3.

Example: "She has been cleaning the room." →"The room has been being cleaned by her."

Why other options are wrong:

(a): Wrong structure and wrong verb form; "has updated" is not continuous and also missing "been/being".

(c): Changes tense to present continuous ("is being updated"), not present perfect continuous.

(d): Changes tense to past continuous ("was being updated"), not present perfect continuous.

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph: 1) Digital maps made travel easier, but they also changed how people pay attention to surroundings. 2) When every turn is dictated, the brain practices less "self-navigation" and remembers fewer landmarks. 3) As a result, some commuters feel disoriented on routes they have taken for months. 4) To rebuild this skill, experts suggest occasionally navigating short trips without live directions.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:

1) Digital maps made travel easier, but they also changed how people pay attention to surroundings.

2) When every turn is dictated, the brain practices less "self-navigation" and remembers fewer landmarks.

3) As a result, some commuters feel disoriented on routes they have taken for months.

4) To rebuild this skill, experts suggest occasionally navigating short trips without live directions.
questions.solution:
Correct order: 1, 2, 3, 4

1 introduces the broad idea: convenience with a hidden cost.

2 explains the mechanism ("When every turn is dictated.."), so it must follow 1.

3 states the outcome ("As a result.."), so it must come after the explanation in 2.

4 suggests a remedy ("To rebuild.."), which naturally closes the paragraph.

Correct option is d because it matches 1 → 2 → 3 → 4.

Rule used: General statement → explanation → result → suggestion.

Example: "Phones help us remember numbers, but we stop memorizing; so recall weakens; so practice helps."

· a is wrong because it starts with the explanation (2) before introducing the topic (1).

· b is wrong because it places the result (3) before giving the mechanism (2).

· c is wrong because it starts with a result (3) without setting context first.

Final correct paragraph order: 1, 2, 3, 4

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. Rohan said to his teacher, "I'll do this project with a heart and a half."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Rohan said to his teacher, "I'll do this project with a heart and a half."

options.text: Rohan told his teacher that he will do that project with a heart and a half.
options.html: Rohan told his teacher that he will do that project with a heart and a half.

options.text: Rohan told his teacher that he would do that project with a heart and a half.
options.html: Rohan told his teacher that he would do that project with a heart and a half.

options.text: Rohan told his teacher that he would be doing that project with a heart and a half.
options.html: Rohan told his teacher that he would be doing that project with a heart and a half.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Future Simple Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Present Conditional Tense.

Future Simple (Subject + will/shall + V1 + object) should be converted into Present Conditional (Subject + would/should + V1 + object).

For example:

He said, "I will be in Kolkata on Friday." (Direct Speech)

He said that he would be in Kolkata on Friday. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'he'.

· The verb 'will do' is changed into 'would do'.

· 'This project' is changed into 'that project'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): Rohan told his teacher that he would do that project with a heart and a half.
